zt_def.title: Z-Transform & z-Plane ROC
zt_def.summary: The discrete-time counterpart of the Laplace Transform, mapping x[n] to the complex z-plane (z = r e^(j w)).
zt_def.introduction: Z-transform is essential for designing digital FIR/IIR filters, analyzing difference equations, and DSP system stability.
zt_def.theory:
**Bilateral Z-Transform**:
$$X(z) = \mathcal{Z}\{x[n]\} = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} x[n] z^{-n} \quad (z = r e^{j \omega})$$

**ROC in z-Plane**: Concentric ring $|z_{min}| < |z| < |z_{max}|$.
- **Causal Signal**: ROC is outside circle $|z| > r_{max}$.
- **Anti-Causal Signal**: ROC is inside circle $|z| < r_{min}$.
- **Stable LTI System**: ROC includes the unit circle $|z| = 1$.
zt_def.derivation:
**LTI System Transfer Function H(z)**:
$$H(z) = \frac{Y(z)}{X(z)} = \frac{\sum_{k=0}^{M} b_k z^{-k}}{1 + \sum_{k=1}^{N} a_k z^{-k}}$$
common_mistakes: Omitting the Region of Convergence (ROC). Two completely different signals (e.g. a^n u[n] vs -a^n u[-n-1]) have identical X(z) algebraic form, distinguished ONLY by ROC!

interview_questions.question: What is the relation between s-plane and z-plane?
interview_questions.answer: z = e^{s T_s}. Left-half s-plane maps inside unit circle |z| < 1. jw-axis maps onto unit circle |z| = 1.

viva_questions.question: When is a discrete-time LTI system stable?
viva_questions.answer: When all poles of H(z) lie strictly inside the unit circle |z| < 1.

zt_def.professor_notes: z-plane unit circle |z|=1 corresponds to s-plane jw-axis!
zt_def.memory_trick: 🧠 **Memory Trick**: **Inside Unit Circle = Stable**. **Outside Circle = Causal ROC**.
